children: The firm saw second-quarter net bookings come in at €389m, above guidance for about €370m, driven by strong demand for Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced as well as other titles in its portfolio of games.
However, looking to the third quarter - which includes the holiday shopping season - and Ubisoft said it expects net bookings of around €250m, well below the €361m expected by analysts.
Ubisoft attributed the decline to a "particularly crowded holiday season". The long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI was released by Rockstar Games - which is owned by
- to critical acclaim this week, and is already estimated to have garnered around $2bn in global sales.

Ubisoft maintained both its full-year and mid-term outlooks, but it was not enough to stop the shares slumping, and by 1245 GMT, the Paris-listed stock had tumbled 15%. The group is forecasting net bookings to fall by a high single-digit percentage in the current year, with the second half set to benefit from the release of Rayman Legends Retold and Just Dance: Decades of Hits.

In January, trading in Ubisoft’s shares had to be briefly suspended after it announced a sweeping overhaul of the business - including splitting into five creative decisions - cancelled titles and slashed guidance. A third was wiped off the company’s value, but co-founder and chief executive Yves Guillemot said the "difficult decisions" were necessary to "reset" the company and called it a "decisive turning point". The business had been rocked by falling revenues and repeated launch delays.
Guillemot said on Friday that "tangible progress" had been made in the first half on the firm’s strategic and operational priorities.

He continued: "Our new operating model is now fully in place, with leadership secured across all creative houses. We remain on track with our cost reduction programme, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organisation as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle.
"By combining our iconic brands and creative talent with a more focused, agile and accountable operating model, we are building a stronger Ubisoft."
